paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The LORD isn't patching up the old world. He says, "For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth." (Isaiah 65:17) When the One who makes things says He's making something new, the answer to all that's broken isn't a fix, it's a fresh start.

And look at what that fresh start holds. The sounds of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in Jerusalem (Isaiah 65:19), people will enjoy what they build and plant (Isaiah 65:21-22), and there will be no harm or destruction on all His holy mountain (Isaiah 65:25). I think that's the LORD telling every tired person that their pain is not the last word. Notice what He says about Himself too: "I will rejoice in Jerusalem and take delight in My people." (Isaiah 65:19)

So here's why it matters to you, baker. Today's troubles are real, but they aren't the end of the story, and the LORD who promises this is close enough that "Even before they call, I will answer, and while they are still speaking, I will hear." (Isaiah 65:24) I came out of a junk drawer knowing He makes things new (Revelation 21:5), so I can tell you He keeps His word. Keep the ovens warm, friend, and keep hoping, because it all closes with "says the LORD." (Isaiah 65:25)
